title: Object-Oriented and Modular Design Rules
purpose: Keep domain modeling, module boundaries, interfaces, and dependency direction maintainable.

rules.statement: Model domain concepts with clear responsibilities and stable boundaries.
Use inheritance only when the relationship is truly substitutable.
Prefer composition for shared behavior when it keeps dependencies simpler.
Encapsulate mutable state and expose intentional methods or properties.
Preserve separation of concerns between domain logic, application workflow, interface code, infrastructure, persistence, and external integrations.
Keep public interfaces small, explicit, and consistent with existing project conventions.
Make dependencies visible through constructors, function arguments, or project conventions rather than hidden global state.
Do not introduce new abstractions unless they reduce real complexity, protect a stable boundary, or match an established project pattern.
